title: What is an Email? - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Email is a way to communicate digitally via the Internet. Users may instantaneously share and receive text, files, photos, and other data between various devices and places. Because of its speed, dependability, and ease of use, it is widely utilised for corporate, professional, and personal communication. Its attributes are:

  • Quick and real-time communication delivery
  • Allows file attachments, including photos, videos, and documents.
  • Can simultaneously deliver messages to several recipients
  • Accessible via the internet from any location
  • Allows communications to be stored and documented.

History

Email (Electronic Mail) was first introduced in the early 1970s as a way to send messages between users on the same computer system. Ray Tomlinson is credited with sending the first networked email and introducing the “@” symbol to separate the user name and domain. Over time, email evolved with the growth of the internet and became a standard communication tool worldwide.

Working

Working of email involves a system of servers and communication protocols that handle sending and receiving messages. When a user sends an email, it is first delivered to a mail server, which then forwards it to the recipient’s mail server. The receiver can access the message using a mail client or a web-based service.

  • Uses SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) to send emails
  • Uses POP3 or IMAP to receive emails
  • Mail servers store and forward messages between users

Although email works efficiently through servers and protocols, its practical use also depends on its advantages and disadvantages.

Components

  • Sender Address: Email ID of the person sending the message
  • Summary Email ID of the recipient
  • Subject: Summary of the email
  • Body: Main content of the message
  • Attachments: Files sent along with the email

Types of Email

Emails can be categorized into different types based on how they are used for communication.

1. General Types

  • Personal Email: Used for communication between individuals
  • Professional Email: Used for formal communication in organizations
  • Marketing Email: Used for advertisements and promotions.
  • Notification Email: Alerts and updates are sent via notification email.

2. Based on Purpose

  • Newsletters: Distributed frequently to provide information, deals, or updates.
  • Onboarding Emails: Assist new customers in understanding a good or service.
  • Transactional Emails: Describe purchases, payments, and confirmations in detail.
  • Plain-Text Emails: Simple emails with just text and no attachments or media.

Popular Email Services

  • Gmail: A popular email service renowned for its robust connection with Google services, vast storage capacity, and easy-to-use interface.
  • Outlook: Professional email service from Microsoft that provides seamless Office support, task management, and calendar integration.
  • Yahoo Mail: An email service with a large storage capacity and features like spam filtering and news integration.
  • ProtonMail: Email service that prioritises privacy and provides secure communication using end-to-end encryption.
  • Zoho Mail: Business-focused email service featuring an easy-to-use interface and robust support for teamwork and professional communication.
